previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old man with alcoholic cirrhosis and a history of pancreatitis was admitted for severe epigastric abdominal pain radiating to the back, nausea, and vomiting. He had recently resumed heavy alcohol use. His presentation and elevated lipase were consistent with acute pancreatitis, and he was managed with NPO status, IV fluids, and pain control. He exhibited signs of alcohol withdrawal, including tremors, and was treated with CIWA protocol without complications. Imaging revealed cirrhosis with portal hypertension and an exophytic liver mass; MRI suggested the mass was a cirrhotic or dysplastic nodule, not hepatocellular carcinoma. His pain improved, diet was advanced, and he remained stable. He was discharged home with a short supply of oxycodone, continued liver and asthma medications, and referrals for alcohol abstinence counseling and specialist follow-up.
problems: Unspecified gastritis and gastroduodenitis, without mention of hemorrhage

Brief Hospital Course:
___, h/o alcohol abuse, liver cirrhosis, pancreatitis p/w 1 
month of worsening epigastric pain.  
 
# Acute on Chronic pancreatitis: 
Patient presented with worsening epigastric pain that radiated 
posteriorly that was most likely chronic pancreatitis (lipase 
80) and was controlled with dilaudid home regimen. He was 
initially started on clears and able to tolerate a regular diet 
by time of discharge. 

# Mild alcoholic hepatitis
He did also have a component of mild alcoholic hepatitis with 
elevate AST > ALT and elevated total bilirubin. AST, ALT down 
trended prior to discharge and total bilirubin somewhat elevated 
at baseline but stabilized at 2.2. Discriminate function 
remained below 32 as such prednisolone treatment was not 
initiated.

# EtOH Withdrawal/abuse: 
Patient was placed on CIWA scale with lorazepam protocol.  He 
did have active DT's with sensation of bugs crawling on his 
hands and feet. He did not have any withdrawal seizures. The 
patient appeared to have insight into his substance abuse 
program voicing interest in outpatient programs in addition to 
plan to trial suboxone per past discussions with PCP. Outpatient 
Alcohol rehabilitation programs were provided with the aid of 
social work consultation including: AA listing for the ___ 
area, BPHC PAATHS contact information and overview, SOAP 
brochure for ___, Outptservices at ___, ___ Outpt 
Services. 

# Asthma Exacerbation with history of intubation:
His asthma exacerbation was treated with Q3 hour albuterol nebs 
that were gradually spaced out. He was also treated with 5 day 
prednisone burst with improvement in his symptoms prior to 
discharge. 

# EtOH Cirrhosis: Well compensated. No evidence of 
encephalopathy or ascites. RUQ did not show evidence of ascites 
or portal vein thrombosis.
